title: International Talents @Unibo - SAT: Scholarships for International Students Enrolling in First and Single Cycle Degree Programmes at Alma Mater Studiorum - Universita di Bologna
legacy_titles: International Talents @Unibo - SAT, a.y. 2024-25 (full published call title: "CALL FOR APPLICATIONS INTERNATIONAL TALENTS @UNIBO - SAT - SCHOLARSHIPS FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS ENROLLING IN FIRST AND SINGLE CYCLE DEGREE PROGRAMMES AT ALMA MATER STUDIORUM - UNIVERSITA DI BOLOGNA IN THE 2024-25 ACADEMIC YEAR")
Bando International Talents @Unibo - SAT (Italian official title)
Unibo Azione 1 / Unibo Azione 2 (direct predecessor scheme that combined full tuition-fee waivers with study grants for international students, superseded by International Talents @Unibo)
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission, including a full tuition fee waiver
funding_type: Fixed study grant + full tuition fee waiver (university-funded)
administering_authority: Alma Mater Studiorum - Universita di Bologna (University of Bologna)
implementing_agency: University of Bologna Student Services Division (ASES), International Desk - applications handled through Studenti Online (studenti.unibo.it) and family financial-status documentation through the ER.GO regional portal
programme_action: International Talents @Unibo - SAT track (open to students matriculating in First and Single Cycle degree programmes)
description: The International Talents @Unibo scheme funds merit-based study grants for international students who matriculate in the first year of a degree programme at the University of Bologna, together with a full tuition fee waiver; recipients pay only the fixed first instalment of EUR 157.04 (regional tax, stamp duty and accident-insurance premium). Eligibility is defined by the place where the access qualification was awarded, not by citizenship: applicants must hold a qualification valid for admission obtained outside the Italian education system or at an Italian School abroad. Selection is made on the SAT (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Maths sections) with a minimum combined score of 950, subject to an ISEE band of EUR 16,000-35,000 and an age limit of under 30 at the application deadline. The most recent call published for first and single cycle degree programmes was the a.y. 2024-25 call, which closed on 31 May 2024; the same award name continues to be used for second-cycle (Laurea Magistrale) calls.

award_types: Merit study grant of EUR 4,500 for one academic year
Full tuition fee waiver for the same academic year (recipients pay only EUR 157.04)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: The 2024-25 first/single-cycle call funded 15 study grants of EUR 4,500 each, awarded for one academic year, with a full tuition fee waiver granted to successful applicants. Grants were allocated by geographical area of the country where the access qualification was awarded: 2 Eastern Europe (EE), 2 North America (NA), 1 Central America (CA), 3 South America (SA), 7 Other countries (AP/OC). Payment was in three instalments of EUR 2,000, EUR 1,500 and EUR 1,000, in October, March and July. For the a.y. 2025-26 second-cycle edition of the same scheme the University published 30 grants of EUR 6,500 per academic year each, awarded for two academic years, also with a full tuition fee waiver.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Art. 1 of the call: 'The study grant may only be renewed for the subsequent academic year through a specific call for applications.' Renewal is therefore not automatic; separate renewal calls have been issued (e.g. the 'International Talents @Unibo - Rinnovo' call for a.y. 2024-25, open to prior Unibo Azione 2 recipients). While holding the award, instalments are conditional on credit thresholds (10 ECTS by 20 February and 30 ECTS by 15 July in the 2024-25 call) and on continued enrolment in course ('in corso').
programme_structure.intake: Annual. The latest published first/single-cycle call (a.y. 2024-25) had an application window of 9 February 2024 to 31 May 2024; the parallel second-cycle call for a.y. 2025-26 ran from 17 January 2025 to 30 May 2025. A separate application to the ER.GO regional scholarship is required independently and deadlines are peremptory.

status_label: Closed - last published first-cycle call closed 31 May 2024
status_note: The most recent call for applications for First and Single Cycle degree programmes (International Talents @Unibo - SAT, a.y. 2024-25) closed on 31 May 2024 at 12:00 CEST. For a.y. 2025-26 the University published only a second-cycle 'International Talents @Unibo - GRE' call (17 January 2025 to 30 May 2025; 30 grants of EUR 6,500 for two academic years); no first-cycle call was published for a.y. 2025-26. As of the verification date of 3 October 2026, no first-cycle call for a.y. 2026-27 had been published on bandi.unibo.it. The scheme itself is not discontinued: a new first-cycle call is expected for the next intake (normally published in January or February with a window running to late May), and applicants should monitor bandi.unibo.it. In parallel, non-EU/EEA applicants can apply to the annual ER.GO regional study grant (borsa di studio) of the Emilia-Romagna Region, which also grants a total tuition-fee exemption; that call closed on 24 August 2026 at 16:00 for a.y. 2026/27 and is expected to reopen for a.y. 2027/28.
verification_notes: All award rules, amounts, thresholds and dates above are taken verbatim from the official University of Bologna call for applications PDF hosted on bandi.unibo.it. Tuition-fee amounts, the fixed first instalment, exemption thresholds and the reduced fixed fee were taken from the official unibo.it fee pages and the official 'Tabella importi massimi 2026-2027' PDF for a.y. 2026/27. Five or more official unibo.it / bandi.unibo.it / er-go.it pages were fetched. No award named 'Unibo per la globalizzazione' could be located on any official unibo.it or bandi.unibo.it page, and no entry-requirement bands on a 85/90/95/100 local scale are published for this award; both are recorded as unverified items. No first-cycle International Talents @Unibo call exists for a.y. 2025-26 or a.y. 2026/27, so the record reflects the latest published first-cycle call (a.y. 2024-25) cross-referenced with current 2026/27 fee rules.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: February to the end of May. The latest published first/single-cycle call ran from 9 February 2024 (12:00 CET) to 31 May 2024 (12:00 CEST); the parallel second-cycle calls ran 11 January-30 April 2024 (GRE), 9 February-31 May 2024 (SAT, first cycle) and 17 January-30 May 2025 (GRE, second cycle).
application_deadline.application_period: 9 February 2024 at 12:00 CET to 31 May 2024 at 12:00 CEST (Art. 5). Family financial-status documentation had to be submitted in the same window, 9 February 2024 to 31 May 2024 at 12:00 CEST (Art. 6).
application_deadline.official_rule: Art. 5 - How to apply: 'You must submit your application between 9 February 2024 at 12:00 CET and 31 May 2024 at 12:00 CEST, strictly through Studenti Online (www.studenti.unibo.it).' Art. 6: 'between 9 February 2024 and 31 May 2024 at 12:00 CEST, you must submit the documents regarding your family's economic situation.' The call also required the official SAT score report to be sent through College Board and received by the University of Bologna no later than 31 May 2024.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The deadline is peremptory: applications on paper, by fax or by e-mail were not accepted, and official SAT scores received after 31 May 2024 were not considered. Financial-status documentation is checked thoroughly by ER.GO, and a negative check means loss of benefits. Next-cycle dates are not yet published; re-verify on bandi.unibo.it before February of the intake year.

programme_duration.official_range: One academic year per award; renewal for the following academic year only through a separate call for applications
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewal is never automatic - Art. 1 states the grant 'may only be renewed for the subsequent academic year through a specific call for applications'. During the award year, each instalment is conditional on earning the published credit thresholds (10 ECTS before 20 February and 30 ECTS before 15 July in the 2024-25 call) and on continued in-course enrolment.

funding.scholarship_type: University-funded merit study grant combined with a full tuition fee waiver
funding.monthly_amount_note: The grant is not paid monthly. In the 2024-25 first-cycle call it was paid in three instalments of EUR 2,000, EUR 1,500 and EUR 1,000, with payment procedures starting in October (or on completion of matriculation, if later), March and July, each lasting 60 days.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel allowance is published in the official call.
funding.fully_funded_note: This is not a full-cost award. The published benefit is a EUR 4,500 study grant plus a full tuition fee waiver; no living allowance, accommodation allowance, travel allowance, installation allowance or health-insurance support is published. Living costs in Bologna must be met from other sources (including the separate ER.GO grant, with which this award is incompatible).

tuition.conditions: Full tuition fee waiver for the academic year of award; recipients pay only EUR 157.04 (regional right-to-study tax EUR 140, stamp duty EUR 16, accident-insurance premium EUR 1.04). If the recipient matriculates in a programme whose fee is higher than the one stated in the application, the difference must be paid. For reference, the official maximum all-inclusive contribution for first-cycle programmes in a.y. 2026/27 is EUR 2,040.00 (net of the fixed instalment), rising to EUR 2,550.00 for Mediation/Translation programmes (Mediazione linguistica interculturale, Traduzione ed interpretazione di trattativa, Comunicazione interlinguistica applicata) and EUR 2,805.00 for Genomics.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published. The award is paid in three lump instalments tied to enrolment and credit thresholds, not as a monthly stipend.

insurance.note: Not published in official source. Recipients remain liable for the EUR 1.04 accident-insurance premium included in the EUR 157.04 fixed instalment.

research_allowance.note: Not applicable to a first-cycle award

accommodation_support.note: Not provided by this award. The call states the grant is compatible with other ER.GO forms of study support such as housing services, which must be applied for separately.

bond.note: No service bond. The award does require continued enrolment and published credit thresholds to release each instalment.

total_estimated_value.note: No official total value figure is published and none is computed here. The official call states 15 study grants of EUR 4,500 each plus a full tuition fee waiver for the a.y. 2024-25 first/single-cycle edition.

coverage: Full tuition fee waiver for the academic year of award (recipients pay only the fixed EUR 157.04 first instalment)
Study grant of EUR 4,500 paid in three instalments (EUR 2,000 / EUR 1,500 / EUR 1,000 in the 2024-25 call)
Compatibility with other ER.GO study support such as housing services

The waiver is tied to the programme stated in the application; matriculating in a higher-fee programme means paying the difference
The award covers one academic year only, and renewal requires a separate call for applications

Incompatible with other Unibo grants for the same purpose (UNICORE, departmental grants, Unibo for Refugees prizes), EMJMD scholarships, and scholarships from ER.GO, MAECI, AICS, Collegio Superiore, CRUI, international cooperation projects and foreign government bodies
Only 15 grants were funded in the latest first/single-cycle edition, allocated by geographical area, so the chance of award is low

eligible_applicants: Students holding a qualification valid for admission to a First or Single Cycle degree programme, awarded by an institution outside the Italian education system or by an Italian School abroad (citizenship is irrelevant)
Students who are not, and have not been, enrolled in a First, Single or Second cycle degree programme at the University of Bologna (careers ended after the 2022-23 academic year still count)
Applicants whose family ISEE is between EUR 16,000 and EUR 35,000, or with an equivalent economic situation where an ISEE cannot be obtained because family income and assets are outside Italy
Applicants who have never received a Unibo Azione 2 study grant
Applicants who are less than 30 years old at the application deadline
Applicants with a minimum SAT score of 950 (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing plus Maths)
final_year_condition: Applicants must hold a qualification valid for admission to the chosen First or Single Cycle degree programme, awarded by an institution outside the Italian education system or by an Italian School abroad (Art. 2, point 1). Final-year secondary-school students are therefore only eligible once they hold that qualification; the call does not publish a separate 'graduating student' provision, so applicants still completing secondary school should confirm their position with the International Desk (internationaldesk@unibo.it).
equivalent_degree_note: Any qualification valid for admission obtained outside the Italian education system is accepted regardless of the applicant's citizenship, and qualifications issued by Italian Schools abroad also qualify. Qualifications issued by institutions of the Republic of San Marino do NOT satisfy this requirement. The admission value of foreign qualifications is assessed separately by the University before matriculation.

age_limit.age_calculation_date: Deadline for submitting applications (31 May 2024 for the latest published first/single-cycle call)
age_limit.official_source: Art. 2, Participation requirements, point 5: 'Be less than 30 years old at the deadline for submitting applications.' Call for applications International Talents @Unibo - SAT, a.y. 2024-25 (bandi.unibo.it)

nationality_quota: No nationality quota: eligibility is defined by where the access qualification was awarded, not by citizenship ('regardless of your citizenship'). Grants were, however, allocated in fixed numbers by geographical area of the country where the qualification was awarded: 2 Eastern Europe (EE), 2 North America (NA), 1 Central America (CA), 3 South America (SA), 7 Other countries (AP/OC) - 15 grants in total. Each applicant's area is determined by the country of the institution awarding the qualification, or of the institution administering the studies if different.

eligibility.citizenship: No restriction. Art. 2, point 1: 'Hold a qualification valid for admission to your chosen First or Single Cycle degree programme, awarded by an institution outside of the Italian education system or by an Italian School abroad... Your citizenship is irrelevant.' Qualifications from the Republic of San Marino do not qualify.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement. Residence abroad or in Italy is irrelevant; however, if the family has income and assets only outside Italy, the ISEE cannot be issued and equivalent financial documentation must be submitted. Students with dual citizenship must specify where family income and assets are held.
eligibility.age_limit: Must be less than 30 years old at the application deadline (Art. 2, point 5).
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Hold a qualification valid for admission to the chosen First or Single Cycle degree programme, obtained outside the Italian education system or at an Italian School abroad.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Minimum SAT score of 950 in the sum of the 'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing' and 'Maths' sections, with the test taken after 31 May 2019. No grade or percentage threshold is published.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: None published. Selection is by standardised test score only.
eligibility.language_requirement: None for the scholarship itself. The call sets no IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, Duolingo or Medium of Instruction requirement; any language requirement belongs to the admission requirements of the individual degree programme.
eligibility.financial_need: Yes, as an eligibility gate rather than a ranking factor: ISEE between EUR 16,000 and EUR 35,000, or an equivalent economic situation for applicants who cannot obtain an ISEE because family income and assets are outside Italy.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Yes. The applicant must not have received a Unibo Azione 2 study grant in the past, and the award is incompatible with other Unibo grants/prizes for the same purpose (including UNICORE and Unibo for Refugees prizes), EMJMD scholarships, and scholarships awarded by ER.GO, MAECI, AICS, Collegio Superiore, CRUI (for holders of international or temporary protection), international cooperation projects in which the University is a partner, and foreign governmental bodies or institutions.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Must not be a student of a First, Single or Second cycle degree programme at the University of Bologna; those whose career in such a programme ended after the 2022-23 academic year are still regarded as students, and withdrawals must have been submitted before the call was published. Payment of the grant is conditional on actual admission and matriculation, including paying the first tuition instalment.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None. Any First or Single Cycle degree programme of the University is eligible, except multiple or joint degree programmes for which tuition fees are payable to a partner university other than the University of Bologna.
eligibility.official_source: Call for applications International Talents @Unibo - SAT, a.y. 2024-25, Art. 1-3 (bandi.unibo.it)

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No percentage or final-grade threshold is published for this award. The only numeric academic criterion is the SAT score (minimum 950 in the sum of Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Maths). Unibo's separate merit-based total exemption, which does use a 110/110 degree mark, applies only to second-cycle (Laurea Magistrale) entrants and not to bachelor's applicants.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Admission to the chosen degree programme is a separate procedure governed by that programme's own call for applications; being admitted does not by itself grant the scholarship, and being awarded the scholarship does not waive the programme's admission requirements.
selection_factors_may_include: SAT score (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing + Maths)
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Selection is purely by standardised test score. No interview, portfolio, essay, recommendation letter, leadership or extracurricular assessment forms part of the published criteria.

english_requirement.test_score_note: The scholarship criterion is the SAT (Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and Maths sections) with a minimum combined score of 950, taken after 31 May 2019. The award call itself publishes no IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, Duolingo or Medium of Instruction requirement; English-language admission requirements are set by the individual degree programme and are separate from the scholarship. Equally, programmes taught in Italian carry an Italian-language requirement set at admission.
accepted_tests: SAT (Scholastic Assessment Test) - sections 'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing' and 'Maths'; the official score report must be sent by the applicant through College Board to the University of Bologna, recipient code 6993

language_of_instruction.language_note: The award call imposes no language-of-instruction restriction, and the University of Bologna offers first-cycle degree programmes taught in Italian and in English (for example European Studies, International Studies, Economics, Politics and Social Sciences, Genomics and Biology of Human and Environmental Health). Language requirements for admission, and the Italian-language requirement for programmes taught in Italian, are set by each programme and are separate from this scholarship.

application_method.application_route: Apply online exclusively through Studenti Online (www.studenti.unibo.it), 'Calls' ('Bandi') section, selecting the 'International Talents @Unibo' call; in parallel submit family financial-status documentation through the ER.GO online services portal. Applications on paper, by fax or by e-mail are not accepted.
application_steps: Register on studenti.unibo.it. International students without an Italian tax code (Codice Fiscale) must use the 'International students registration' section; personal details must match the passport exactly.
After first access, replace the PUK code with a personal password and keep the Unibo credentials for the whole study career.
Visit studenti.unibo.it, click 'Calls' ('Bandi') and select the 'International Talents @Unibo - SAT, a.y. 2024-25' call (only applicants meeting Art. 2 points 2 and 5 can proceed).
Check contact details and enter the required details, including the correct geographical area of the country where the access qualification was awarded.
Upload the required documents in PDF: a copy of a valid passport (EU citizens may attach a copy of a valid identity document) and a copy of the unofficial SAT score report.
Send the official SAT score report through College Board to the University of Bologna (recipient code 6993); it must be received by the University no later than 31 May 2024.

Submit the ISEE certificate for higher-education subsidies, or the equivalent financial-status documentation for families with income and/or assets abroad, via the ER.GO portal within the same window.
Confirm acceptance by e-mail to internationaldesk@unibo.it within 10 days of the award notification.
application_method.application_fee: No scholarship application fee is charged. Enrolment requires payment of the first tuition instalment (EUR 157.04), and recipients must pay it before the first grant instalment is released.

selection_process.decision_maker: University of Bologna - Student Services Division (ASES); ranking lists are approved by decree of the Head of Division
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive merit ranking by standardised test score
possible_stages: Online application through Studenti Online with document upload
Receipt of the official SAT score report through College Board
Submission of financial-status documents through the ER.GO portal
Administrative verification of applications after the deadline by the competent offices
Creation of a general ranking list and one ranking list per geographical area, ranked in decreasing order of score
Approval of the ranking lists by decree of the Head of Division and publication on studenti.unibo.it
Notification of winners by e-mail and confirmation of acceptance within 10 days
selection_process.weighting_note: No percentage weighting is published. Applicants are ranked in decreasing order of SAT score and, in case of a tie, preference is given to the younger applicant. Grants allocated to each geographical area are awarded from that area's ranking list, and any residual grants from the general ranking list.
selection_process.results_timing: Ranking lists are published on www.studenti.unibo.it after the deadline has expired and after the competent offices have verified the applications. Winners are notified by e-mail and must confirm acceptance within 10 days. Study grants are paid in three instalments with procedures starting in October (or on completion of matriculation, if later), March and July, each lasting 60 days.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Two parallel rankings exist: a general ranking list and one for each geographical area (Eastern Europe, North America, Central America, South America, Other countries AP/OC). Withdrawals received by 15 July 2024 allow reassignment to the next suitable applicant in the same area's ranking list and then in the general list.

additional_factors: Geographical area of the country where the access qualification was awarded (determines the quota of grants available to the applicant)
Age, used only as a tie-breaker with preference for the younger applicant
selection_criteria.source: Financial need functions only as an eligibility gate (ISEE between EUR 16,000 and EUR 35,000, or equivalent); ranking is by SAT score alone. Source: Call for applications International Talents @Unibo - SAT, a.y. 2024-25, Art. 2, Art. 4 and Art. 7.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: First cycle degree (Laurea) or single cycle degree (Laurea Magistrale a Ciclo Unico) of the Alma Mater Studiorum - Universita di Bologna
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 3 years for first cycle (Laurea) degrees; 5-6 years for single cycle degrees such as Medicine and Surgery, Law, Pharmacy, Architecture, Veterinary Medicine and Dentistry
possible_awards: Laurea Magistrale a Ciclo Unico (single cycle degree)
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship is tied to matriculation, that is the first enrolment in the first year of a degree programme. Enrolling in years after the first, changing programme or transferring from another university does not count as matriculation, and study grants may not be awarded to students enrolling in multiple or joint degree programmes whose tuition is payable to a partner university other than the University of Bologna.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Credits earned during the award year must be earned at the University of Bologna or at another university within a mobility programme in which the University of Bologna participates; payment procedures start only after the credit-recognition process is completed. In case of matriculation in a shortened programme, credits recognised from the previous career are valid for the purposes of the call. Unrecognised credits from single course units, credits from Italian-language courses at the University Language Centre (CLA) and other credits not counting towards the qualification are not taken into account.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Full tuition fee waiver for the academic year of award. Recipients pay only the fixed first instalment of EUR 157.04, corresponding to the regional right-to-study tax of EUR 140, stamp duty of EUR 16 and accident-insurance premium of EUR 1.04. If the recipient matriculates in a programme with a higher fee than the one stated in the application, the difference must be paid.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No scholarship application fee. A tuition instalment of EUR 157.04 must be paid to enrol, and must be paid before the first grant instalment is released.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: No student agreement or return-of-service contract is published for this award.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Recipients keep access to the University's student services and to other ER.GO forms of study support such as housing services. Accommodation, canteen and transport concessions are applied for separately. The award is incompatible with the scholarship programmes listed in Art. 3 of the call.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No service bond. Failure to meet the published credit thresholds means the corresponding instalment is not paid (although later attainment of a subsequent threshold triggers payment of the missed instalments too). If ER.GO's checks on financial-status documents are negative, the benefits obtained are revoked and any amount already received must be returned.

application_readiness_checklist: Book and sit the SAT early enough for the official score report to reach the University of Bologna (recipient code 6993) before 31 May

Obtain the secondary-school qualification valid for admission outside the Italian education system (or at an Italian School abroad) and confirm its admission value with the University before matriculating
Identify the country of the institution awarding the access qualification, since this determines the geographical area quota applied for
Gather family income and asset documentation covering income and assets abroad and, where applicable, the Italian ISEE with the INPS DSU protocol number
Register on studenti.unibo.it as an international student without a Codice Fiscale and keep the credentials
Confirm being under 30 at the application deadline and not previously a University of Bologna student
Check that the chosen programme is not a multiple or joint degree whose fees are payable to another university
Plan for cash: the grant is not paid until October, March or July, and the first tuition instalment must be paid first
programme_comparison_fields: Whether a full tuition fee waiver is included
Entry test required and minimum score
Number of awards and geographical-area quotas
Compatibility with ER.GO, MAECI and national scholarships
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No motivation letter, personal statement or interview is required for this award. Effort should go into maximising the SAT score and into assembling a clean, consistent financial documentation set, because administrative checks by ER.GO are the main cause of lost benefits.
profile_fit_labels: Non-EU/EEA applicant with a foreign secondary-school qualification
Middle-income family (ISEE or equivalent between EUR 16,000 and EUR 35,000)
First-time university entrant, not previously enrolled at the University of Bologna
common_mistakes: Assuming the award is based on nationality rather than on where the access qualification was awarded
Relying on the unofficial SAT score only and letting the College Board official report arrive after the deadline
Indicating the wrong geographical area, which is checked at matriculation and can cause loss of benefits
Treating admission to the degree programme as automatic scholarship eligibility, or vice versa
Failing to submit financial-status documents in the same window as the application
Assuming the grant covers living costs, accommodation or travel, which it does not
Assuming automatic renewal in the following year; a new call is required
Ignoring the incompatibility list and also applying to ER.GO, MAECI or other overlapping schemes

risk_flags.risk: No first-cycle International Talents @Unibo call has been published for a.y. 2025-26 or a.y. 2026/27, so the route may be dormant or replaced
risk_flags.impact: Applicants may plan around an award that is not currently open for bachelor's entry
risk_flags.mitigation: Monitor bandi.unibo.it and the University's Study grants and subsidies page from January each year, and apply in parallel to the annual ER.GO regional study grant, which grants a total tuition-fee exemption and reopened most recently on 24 August 2026

risk_flags.risk: Very small number of awards (15 grants in the latest first-cycle edition) allocated across five geographical areas
risk_flags.impact: High rejection rate even for well-qualified applicants
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the award as a supplement, not a funding plan; secure other funding, including the reduced fixed fee for citizens of particularly poor/developing or non-OECD countries

risk_flags.risk: Incompatibility with the ER.GO regional study grant, MAECI scholarships and other national or university grants
risk_flags.impact: Accepting this award can block access to larger or longer-running funding
risk_flags.mitigation: Compare the value of each option before accepting; the award is compatible with ER.GO non-monetary support such as housing services

risk_flags.risk: Financial-status documents are audited by ER.GO and a negative check revokes benefits
risk_flags.impact: Grant clawback and loss of the tuition waiver
risk_flags.mitigation: Submit complete and accurate income and asset documentation covering all foreign and Italian sources, and disclose dual-citizenship income positions

risk_flags.risk: The tuition waiver is tied to the programme named in the application
risk_flags.impact: Matriculating in a higher-fee programme means paying the difference out of pocket
risk_flags.mitigation: Notify internationaldesk@unibo.it of any programme change before matriculation and budget for the fee difference

risk_flags.risk: Instalments depend on credit thresholds (10 ECTS by February and 30 ECTS by July in the 2024-25 call) and on in-course enrolment
risk_flags.impact: Late or missing payments if credits are not earned on schedule
risk_flags.mitigation: Register for enough exams early in the year and check credit recognition through the Student Administration Office

risk_flags.risk: Renewal is not automatic and requires a new call for applications
risk_flags.impact: Years 2 and 3 of the degree are unfunded unless a renewal call is issued
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply to each renewal call as published and plan a fallback such as the ER.GO grant, the reduced fixed fee, or the ISEE-based total exemption (EUR 157.04 only, for ISEE at or below EUR 27,000 plus 10 ECTS by 10 August)

risk_flags.risk: Age limit of under 30 at the application deadline and exclusion of anyone with a prior University of Bologna career
risk_flags.impact: Older applicants and former Unibo students are excluded even if otherwise qualified
risk_flags.mitigation: Check both conditions before investing in SAT preparation; former Unibo students should instead pursue the ER.GO grant or the ISEE/merit-based total exemption

database_notes: Substitution note: no substitution was required. The target scholarship is a University of Bologna merit-based award for international undergraduate students and is not on the DO-NOT-DUPLICATE list in research/bachelor/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md.

The award was renamed and restructured over time. The current scheme is 'International Talents @Unibo'; its direct predecessors were 'Unibo Azione 1' (tuition-fee-only waivers) and 'Unibo Azione 2' (study grants), which were combined in the Unibo Action 1&2 calls of 2018-2023.

The latest published call for First and Single Cycle degree programmes is the a.y. 2024-25 call, whose official deadline of 31 May 2024 is used as application_deadline.deadline_date with deadline_precision 'exact'. Because that date is earlier than the verification date of 2026-10-03, status is 'CLOSED' and the next cycle is described in status_note.
The name 'Unibo per la globalizzazione' given in the research brief could not be found on any official unibo.it or bandi.unibo.it page, and no such programme is recorded here.
No entry-requirement bands on an 85/90/95/100 local scale are published for this award. The research brief's assumption could not be confirmed and has not been reproduced.

The research brief's stated application windows of 'February-March and May-June' do not match the official published windows (9 February to 31 May for the first-cycle call; 17 January to 30 May for the 2025-26 second-cycle call). Official windows are used.
No IELTS/TOEFL/MOI requirement exists for this scholarship. Language requirements are part of admission to individual programmes and are not published in the scholarship call.

The 'national merit waiver' referred to as 'Borsa di studio Merito' on university.it could not be verified as an official source: university.it is not an official Italian government or university domain. In Italy the right-to-study scholarship (borsa di studio) is administered regionally, so for Bologna it is ER.GO's call, which is cross-referenced here.

Unibo's own named 'Total merit-based exemption' page (110/110 degree mark, automatic at enrolment, EUR 157.04 payable) applies only to students entering the FIRST YEAR OF SECOND CYCLE degree programmes who graduated from a Unibo first-cycle degree in a.y. 2025/26 by 31 July 2026 (30 November 2026 for healthcare professions). It therefore does not create a bachelor's entry right and is recorded only as context.

For bachelor's applicants the relevant merit-linked total exemption is the ISEE-based one: full exemption from the variable part (paying only EUR 157.04) where the family financial index is at or below EUR 27,000, and, from the second year onwards, only with 10 ECTS earned between 11 August 2025 and 10 August 2026 for the second year or 25 ECTS for years after the second. Partial exemption applies where the index is above EUR 27,000.

Tuition-fee amounts quoted are the official maximum all-inclusive contributions for a.y. 2026/27 published in the University's 'Tabella importi massimi 2026-2027' PDF, which is net of the regional tax, stamp duty and insurance premium. First-cycle programmes: standard EUR 2,040.00; Mediazione linguistica interculturale, Traduzione ed interpretazione di trattativa and Comunicazione interlinguistica applicata EUR 2,550.00; Genomics EUR 2,805.00. Single-cycle programmes: standard EUR 2,244.00; Medicine and Surgery EUR 3,315.00; Pharmacy EUR 3,060.00; Veterinary Medicine EUR 3,315.00; Odontoiatria e protesi dentaria EUR 4,080.00; Conservazione e restauro dei beni culturali EUR 5,916.00.

The maximum fee is a single annual figure and is not differentiated by course year on the official table. Differentiation by year of course arises through the exemption and credit rules, and through the fixed-instalment structure, rather than through separate maxima per year.

The reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) is a nationality-based discount, not a merit award, and is incompatible with the ISEE-based total or partial exemption. It is recorded here only as the fallback route for non-EU/non-OECD citizens. For a.y. 2026/27: citizens of particularly poor and developing countries pay EUR 500 plus EUR 157.04 as freshmen or with the minimum credits (EUR 600 plus EUR 157.04 without), and citizens of non-OECD countries pay EUR 1,000 plus EUR 157.04 (EUR 1,200 plus EUR 157.04 without).
The €157.04 first instalment is not a university fee and is always payable, including by fully exempt students and by recipients of the ER.GO scholarship.

The scholarship call and the ER.GO study-grant call are mutually exclusive: accepting International Talents @Unibo blocks the ER.GO grant, which is larger and longer-running for most applicants. This is flagged in risk_flags.
The English version of the call is provided for information purposes only; only the Italian version is valid for implementation, dispute resolution and all other legal purposes.

Completeness score 0.87 reflects that every required key is populated from official sources, but that the latest first-cycle call is two admission cycles old, no next-cycle dates are published, several benefit categories are genuinely not published by the University, and three of the research brief's named assumptions ('Unibo per la globalizzazione', 85/90/95/100 bands, February-March and May-June windows, IELTS/TOEFL/MOI) could not be confirmed on official sources.
